transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-15 14:30 PT • Duration: 52m • Attendees: Miguel (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Avery (Redwood CSM), Dana (Helium Head of ML), Ethan (Helium Platform), Sofia (CFO), Mark (SRE)

Summary (auto): Quick Q4 checkpoint. Discussed cost bump during Black Friday-ish spike, tails of latency for large chat sessions, and plan for rightsize pilot and security docs.

[00:00] Miguel: hey everyone, thanks for making time today, uh we'll do a quick health check for q4, get aligned on next steps for the rightsize pilot and security items. how's that sound?

[00:12] Dana: sounds good, Miguel. quick context — traffic peaked mid-November with a few sustained hours of 2.5x baseline, so we saw cost jump. want to understand where to prune or move to dedicated capacity.

[00:26] Priya: yeah, and hi Dana — before we jump in, can you confirm the SLAs you need for the paid tier? you mentioned p99 under 400ms previously?

[00:33] Dana: correct, p99 around 350-400ms for short-chat flows, longer context okay to be a bit higher but must not block UX.

[00:40] Ethan: we also have a retention/PII constraint — some tokens must never be logged or stored outside our VPC. that steers us toward Private or very strict hosted controls.

[00:51] Miguel: got it. two buckets then: econ (cost) and compliance (data residency/KMS). we'll cover routing options that balance them.

[01:05] Priya: quick note on the cost spike — from our initial look at the logs you sent, a lot of the extra cost came from a small subset of long-rolling sessions and repeated re-runs of the same prompt by a test harness. there may be simple fixes like prefix caching and rate-limiting to reduce token churn.

[01:25] Dana: hmm, ok, the re-runs were from a third-party integration that was misconfigured — sorry about that. but the long sessions are real, that's our diagnostic flows.

[01:35] Miguel: absolutely. two levers: model-level (quantize, lean model family) and infra-level (dedicated pool with reserved GPUs + autoscale). for Helium's usage profile, a short-term rightsize pilot can show cost delta.

[01:50] Sofia: from finance side, predictable spend is the priority. we can do reserved if the unit-economics work — but need a clear forecast.

[02:02] Priya: for forecast we propose: 1) run a 7-day mock benchmark that replays real traffic and measures per-token cost under three configs: hosted standard, hosted with KV/prefix cache, and Dedicated with quantized model. 2) we return a CSV with latency distributions and token cost.

[02:24] Mark: what's the operational lift for Dedicated? do we have to manage updates?

[02:30] Miguel: minimal on your side — Redwood manages the runtime. You can pin model versions, and we offer rolling canaries for model rollout. The only infra piece is peering (VPC) and optional KMS integration if you want private key control.

[02:45] Ethan: about KMS — we prefer to keep keys in our provider HSM; will that work?

[02:51] Priya: yes, we integrate with common KMS/HSM providers via customer-managed keys. We'll need your KMS vendor and network diagram for the security checklist.

[03:05] Dana: good. can you talk through quantization tradeoffs? we tested an 8-bit variant in-house and saw some drop in hallucination on a synthetic eval.

[03:16] Priya: sure — quantization often reduces token cost and memory pressure but can change output distribution. our Optimize team recommends targeted quant profiles: 8-bit for high-throughput, but keep full-precision for judgment-heavy paths. We can set routing by endpoint: small model for low-latency stateless queries, full-precision for risky prompts.

[03:42] Miguel: also worth mentioning automatic fallbacks — if a quantized path shows low confidence, Redwood can route to the full model and surface the unit cost difference.

[03:53] Sofia: how do you surface cost at the token level? we need line-item billing by route and model.

[03:59] Avery: console provides token-level breakdown per route and per model, with daily CSV export. we'll include example exports in the worksheet we send.

[04:12] Ethan: latency tails — we saw some p99 spikes at 1.2s when KV cache misses occurred. how do we mitigate misses?

[04:20] Priya: two things: smarter prefix/KV caching based on session heuristics and continuous batching settings tuned to your seq-length distribution. For your diagnostic flows, we might increase cache TTL for in-session prefixes and reduce batching windows for interactive flows.

[04:40] Dana: can the caching be per-customer/route? we have enterprise customers with different patterns.

[04:46] Priya: yes, cache scoping by route or token-group is supported. You can also set eviction policies per route.

[05:00] Miguel: quick commercial note — Dedicated pricing gives predictable unit cost but requires a commit; Hosted with routing can be cheaper short-term but more variable. We'll model both in the worksheet.

[05:12] Sofia: what's a typical commit level for a company our size? approx GPUs?

[05:18] Miguel: for Helium's 2.5x spikes and avg throughput, typical starting commitment is 4–8 V100-equivalent GPUs or similar across GPUs; we'll size precisely after the 7-day benchmark.

[05:31] Mark: and upgrades? autoscale bursts?

[05:35] Priya: Dedicated includes burst capacity options to handle unexpected peaks; on-hosted we can also do cross-region fallback to maintain availability.

[05:44] Dana: security checklist — we've flagged SOC2 activity and network/peering. do you have a template?

[05:50] Avery: yes, we'll send a SOC2 evidence pack, the private deployment spec, and a sample network diagram. we also need your list of vendors and your SOC2 in-scope systems.

[06:02] Ethan: noted. I'll pull a VPC peering diagram and KMS vendor by end of next week.

[06:09] Priya: ok, timeline suggestion: bench this week (if you can give traffic logs), bench complete by Dec 22, Redwood returns the CSV and cost model Dec 23–24, then pilot kickoff after holidays week of Jan 4.

[06:26] Dana: Dec 22 is tight but we can try; the team has a freeze Dec 20–21 for holidays. can we do bench the wk of Dec 28 instead?

[06:34] Miguel: yes, that works — we can shift. important is we get a 7-day representative sample.

[06:42] Sofia: last question: any red flags on vendor lock with Dedicated? we want flexibility to revert to Hosted.

[06:49] Priya: no vendor lock — models and configs are portable, and we support automated export/import of keys/configs. rollback and fallback policies are standard.

[06:58] Miguel: ok let's recap action items and owner: Priya will run bench and produce CSV; Miguel will produce cost worksheet and routing recommendations; Ethan will send infra diagrams and KMS vendor; Avery will send SOC2 docs and sample console exports.

[07:18] Dana: perfect. one last thing — can you include a sample canary rollout plan? we have strict customer-facing release windows.

[07:27] Miguel: yes we'll include a templated canary with percentage ramp and automatic fallback thresholds.

[07:34] Mark: also include alert hooks that tie into our PagerDuty — we need clear SLO breach triggers.

[07:40] Avery: noted, we'll include webhook examples and SLO metrics.

[07:47] Miguel: great, thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the worksheet and timeline in an email.

[07:54] Dana: thanks — appreciate the alignment.

End: quick recap, next steps as above.

Notes: minor transcription errors likely — names sometimes garbled. references: attached files to follow: "Helium_traffic_histogram_202611.zip" (link shared in Slack), "Redwood_rightsize_worksheet_template.csv" (to be sent), SOC2 evidence pack link (Avery).
